# Burn Rate Index

**How many foreign components Russia fires each month in Shahed-type drones, compared with what it loses on the battlefield and how it replaces it.**

**Live dashboard:** https://thomasdido08-code.github.io/burn-rate-index/
**Author:** Thomas Di Domenico

<!-- HEADLINE:START (generated by scripts/build.py, do not edit by hand) -->
**October 2026: 813,503 foreign component records fired** (−6% on September 2026), 97,384 of them from EU-owned firms.

From January 2025 to October 2026, Shahed-type launches carried an estimated 12.5M foreign component records (range 3.3M to 17.7M), 1.6M from EU-owned firms: about 874 times the records in every matched platform Russia lost over the same period, even if each were rebuilt new.
<!-- HEADLINE:END -->

## What this measures

Russia's war effort runs on two different kinds of demand for foreign electronics:

- **What it loses.** Tanks, armoured vehicles, artillery and drones destroyed or captured on the battlefield. Russia has replaced most of its lost armour by pulling Soviet-era vehicles out of storage. That stock is finite: satellite counts show about 28% of the pre-war tank stock still in storage in June 2026, and fewer than a thousand tanks judged restorable.
- **What it fires.** Every Shahed-type drone launched has to be replaced with a new one, built from new components, many of them made by Western firms and reaching Russia through third countries.

The **Burn Rate Index** measures the second kind: the foreign component records carried by the Shahed-type drones Russia launches in a month. It moves with how much Russia fires, and so with how many foreign parts it has to keep sourcing. The finding is that firing, not losing, drives Russia's demand for foreign components by a wide margin.

## How the index is calculated

```
index(month) = launches × [ strike share × foreign records per Shahed-136
                          + (1 − strike share) × foreign records per Gerbera decoy ]
```

- **Launches**: monthly Shahed-type launches reported by the Ukrainian Air Force, as compiled by the Institute for Science and International Security (ISIS).
- **Strike share**: ISIS's estimate of the share of launches that were strike drones rather than decoys.
- **Foreign records per unit**: components that Ukraine's military intelligence (GUR) documented in one teardown of each drone type and attributed to manufacturers headquartered outside Russia and Belarus.

A component **record** is one entry in GUR's database. GUR records no quantities, and one part type can appear more than once, so the index measures dependence on foreign components, not a count of chips. The EU-owned figure counts records whose manufacturer's parent group is headquartered in the EU, which says nothing about where the part was made or how it reached Russia.

Full detail, assumptions and limitations: [METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md).

## Main limitations

- **One teardown per type.** Component records come from a single GUR teardown of each weapon; later production batches may differ.
- **Decoy share is estimated.** Months without an ISIS strike share use ISIS's last monthly share. The low and high bounds (all decoys, all Shaheds) are published alongside.
- **Jet drones are not split out.** Jet-powered Geran-3s are counted with the Shahed-136's 155 foreign records, though GUR found 44 in a Geran-3. Months with many jets are overstated.
- **Losses are a floor.** WarSpotting counts only losses confirmed by photo or video, and footage of recent months keeps surfacing.
- **Storage counts come from one analyst** (Jompy), from satellite imagery. Vehicles kept under roofs are not visible.
- **Missiles and glide bombs are not in the index**, because monthly counts by type are not published for the whole period. In October 2025, the one month with published figures, they would have added about 15%.

## Repository layout

```
index.html                      the dashboard (GitHub Pages serves it)
data/raw/                       source data, one file per source (see data/README.md)
data/derived/
  burn_rate_monthly.csv         the index, month by month, with low/high bounds
  headline.json                 the headline figures
scripts/build.py                recomputes data/derived and the headline above
scripts/fetch_warspotting.py    downloads WarSpotting's loss records (see UPDATING.md)
scripts/aggregate_losses.py     rebuilds the two loss files from that download
UPDATING.md                     the monthly update procedure
METHODOLOGY.md                  full method, assumptions and limitations
assets/                         bundled d3 library
```

## Reproduce

Requires Python 3 only (no packages):

```
python scripts/build.py
```

To view the dashboard locally, run `python -m http.server` in the repository folder and open http://localhost:8000.
